anatomy: Tiredness can affect daily tasks. Tell the team if it worsens or comes with dizziness, reduced eating or other new symptoms.
Hair may thin or fall out. Ask about scalp care, sun protection and practical support; the timing of recovery varies.
Taste may change or disappear, making food less appealing. Report reduced intake early and ask for dietitian help.
A rash with blistering, peeling, mouth sores or fever needs urgent assessment. Keep scheduled skin reviews and report new lesions.
Cramps and muscle pain are common concerns. Severe pain, weakness or dark urine needs urgent advice; do not add supplements or medicines yourself.
Nausea, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Call if symptoms persist, you cannot drink or urine becomes reduced.
Taste changes and poor appetite can cause weight loss. Keep a practical eating plan and tell the team about loose clothes or falling weight.
A strict pregnancy-prevention programme applies to women and men, with restrictions continuing after treatment. Report possible exposure immediately.
Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual itching or upper-abdominal pain. Keep the planned liver blood tests; a symptom needs assessment rather than self-diagnosis.
At 38°C or above, hold both medicines and contact the team under your fever plan. Infection and dehydration must also be considered.
Report blurred vision, eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or a change in sight promptly; some eye problems need urgent specialist treatment.
Keep ECG and heart ultrasound checks. New breathlessness, swollen ankles, palpitations or chest pain needs prompt assessment.
Rash and skin sensitivity may occur; new changing spots need review. Blistering, peeling or mouth sores with a rash needs urgent help.
Liver changes may first appear in blood tests. Report yellow eyes or skin, dark urine, unusual itching or upper-abdominal pain.
Fever, vomiting or diarrhoea can cause dehydration and kidney problems. Call for reduced urine, dizziness or inability to keep fluids down.
Aches can occur. Severe muscle pain or weakness, especially with dark urine, needs urgent advice and possible blood tests.
Tell the team about persistent diarrhoea, vomiting or pain. Severe abdominal pain, blood or black stools needs urgent assessment.
Fatigue and headache can occur. Fever, marked weakness, dizziness or new neurological symptoms needs advice; do not assume it is a harmless drug effect.
Blurred vision, spots, altered colour vision or eye pain needs prompt assessment. Retinal problems may occur with binimetinib.
Keep ECG and heart-pumping checks. Report palpitations, fainting, swollen ankles or new breathlessness; severe chest pain is an emergency.
Report new growths or changes in existing spots and attend skin checks. Severe rash, blistering or peeling needs urgent help.
Liver changes may have no early symptoms, so attend monthly tests. Report yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or upper-abdominal pain.
Kidney tests accompany CK monitoring. Reduced urine, dehydration or dark urine with muscle symptoms needs urgent advice.
CK can rise before or with muscle injury. Report muscle pain, weakness or dark urine, and keep the planned blood tests.
Nausea and diarrhoea may occur. Persistent vomiting, inability to drink, severe abdominal pain, black stools or bleeding needs assessment.
New severe headache, visual change, unusual tiredness, dizziness, thirst or frequent urination may signal immune effects and needs prompt advice.
New cough or breathlessness may reflect lung inflammation or another serious cause. Call promptly; severe breathing difficulty is an emergency.
Chest pain, palpitations, marked muscle weakness or swallowing difficulty can be serious immune effects. Seek urgent assessment.
Inflammation may first show in blood tests. Report yellow eyes or skin, dark urine, unusual itching or upper-abdominal pain.
Kidney inflammation may be detected on blood tests. Report reduced urine, swelling, blood in urine or a marked change from normal.
